chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abi Basir, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them), who said:

Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, concealed four things within four other things: He concealed His Pleasure in His Obedience, so do not underestimate any act of obedience, for perhaps it coincides with His Pleasure while you do not know it. And He concealed His Wrath in His Disobedience, so do not underestimate any act of disobedience, for perhaps His Disobedience coincides with His Wrath while you do not know it. And He concealed His Response in His Supplication, so do not underestimate any supplication, for perhaps it coincides with His Response while you do not know it. And He concealed His Friend among His Servants, so do not underestimate any servant of God, for perhaps he is His Friend while you do not know it.
ai.seo_question: What four things did God conceal within other things according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith outlines the principle of *khafiyyat* (hidden realities), teaching that divine pleasure, wrath, acceptance of prayer, and the presence of *awliya* are concealed within their respective domains. It serves as an ethical exhortation to avoid underestimating minor acts of obedience or disobedience, as they may carry significant spiritual weight unknown to the observer. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawassul* and the spiritual status of the Imams and righteous servants, who are often unrecognized by the general public.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-31 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqy, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather Al-Hassan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abi Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of his father the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB), “

The Blessed the Sublime God has embedded four things in four other things. He has embedded His Pleasure in His obedience. Therefore, you should not underestimate obedience to God. It may cause God’s Pleasure while you do not know it. God has embedded His Wrath in disobeying Him. Therefore, you should not underestimate any disobedience to God. It may cause God’s Wrath while you do not know about it. God has embedded His Response to supplications. Therefore, you should not underestimate any supplications. It may cause God to respond to you while you do not know about it. God has embedded His Friends amongst His Servants. Therefore, you should not belittle anyone, since he may be a friend of God and you may not know about it.”
